records.name: Jebel Irhoud

scene_date.time_system: years ago, as reported by the archaeological study; do not convert into an exact BCE year
scene_date.qualification: Endpoints are arithmetic around the published estimate, not a claim that occupation lasted throughout this interval. The abstract does not define the uncertainty confidence level.

location.qualification: Rounded from a fossil-locality record explicitly derived from a nearby landmark. It is not a verified excavation coordinate. Only a broad overview marker/halo is justified; gate any close-up pin until a primary site survey is checked.
location.certainty: General locality supported; exact excavation point unresolved.

narration.text: At Jebel Irhoud in present-day Morocco, early Homo sapiens remains occur with Middle Stone Age tools dated to about 300,000 years ago.
This is one part of a much wider African story of human origins.
narration.qualification: Do not depict a unique birthplace or a documented route from this site to all later populations.

visual.allowed: Archaeological site symbol or locality halo

records.name: Meroe / Kush
records.feature_type: royal city with separate funerary landscape

scene_date.qualification: Use a generic royal-pyramid scene in the documented third-century burial phase. This is not the beginning or duration of Kush. Do not assign a precise construction year to an unnamed pyramid.

location.precision: North and South cemeteries, Meroe 2 component representative point
location.certainty: Cemetery complex identified; not an individual pyramid footprint.
location.qualification: Keep city label/seat and cemetery schematic distinct at close zoom. UNESCO maps page rounds points to [33.7166667,16.9333333] and [33.75,16.9333333]; nomination gives more specific component points, not survey guarantees.

narration.text: Meroe was a major centre of Kush. From the third century BCE, most Kushite rulers were buried here.
Its royal cemeteries used steep-sided pyramids above tombs cut into the ground.

visual.allowed: Original generic Kushite funerary pyramid schematic

monument.form: Square-based, steep-sided pyramid with a small chapel on its eastern side; no copied relief, photograph or reconstructed specific tomb.
monument.dating_locator: PDF pages 35 and 42; third-century BCE royal burials with pyramid superstructures
monument.qualification: Construction interval belongs to the class/phase. Render as a schematic example, not a measured reconstruction or a dated named pyramid.

avoid: Meroe pyramids appearing at 800 BCE merely because Kush already existed
empty triangular outline implying a chamber inside the pyramid

Some turned a single block of stone into the image of a many-storeyed building.

narration.text: Kilwa Kisiwani was a Swahili trading city, especially prosperous in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
Its merchants connected African hinterland goods with Indian Ocean markets in Arabia, India and China.
